data.title: Police made 1,314 arrests in France's protests: government
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Police arrested 1,314 people in weekend protests across France, the interior ministry said Sunday, adding that 53 officers were hurt in clashes.

data.title: Demonstrators wounded as Portugal police clear housing protest camps
data.description: MADRID - Portuguese police again cleared tents set up by protesters against skyrocketing housing prices overnight Sunday, with organisers criticising the brutality of the officers involved.

data.title: CP distances itself, chairman from holy basil patents
data.description: Charoen Pokphand Group (CP), the country’s largest agribusiness conglomerate, has distanced itself and its senior chairman Dhanin Chearavanont from the controversial patents registered for new varieties of holy basil, a popular herb in Thai cuisine.

data.title: Black, spotted leopards filmed together in Kaeng Krachan
data.description: A wildlife photographer has reported seeing two black and three spotted leopards together on a road in Kaeng Krachan National Park, highlighting the ecological richness of the Unesco World Heritage forest.

data.title: Black, spotted leopards filmed togrther in Kaeng Krachan
data.description: A wildlife photographer has reported seeing two black and three spotted leopards together on a road in Kaeng Krachan National Park, highlighting the ecological richness of the Unesco World Heritage forest.

data.title: Traffic police ordered to unmask, start with warnings, not take bribes
data.description: Traffic police nationwide have been ordered to always show their face when disciplining motorists, to start with warnings before progressive fines, and not to take proffered bribes.

data.title: Domestic flyers also subject to new luggage search rule
data.description: Travellers on all domestic flights are also liable to have their luggage searched under new regulations, not just flyers leaving the kingdom, the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) warned on Sunday.

data.title: Flooding persists in Bangkok, 17 provinces, toll at 83
data.description: Flooding persisted in parts of Bangkok and in 17 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but water levels were declining, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation reported on Sunday.

data.title: Serbia votes with ruling party facing ascendant student movement
data.description: BELGRADE - Polls opened in Serbia on Sunday in what is set to be its most fiercely contested parliamentary election in more than 14 years, as a student-led movement seeks to oust the party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic.

data.title: WHO backs ThaiHealth funding and tobacco and alcohol tax safeguards
data.description: The World Health Organization has asked Thailand to safeguard ThaiHealth funding and maintain the overall tax burden on tobacco and alcohol during a financing review.

data.title: B40/day fare on Red, Purple lines likely to be extended
data.description: The Transport Ministry will propose the extension of the 40-baht day-tripper rate on the two Red Lines and the Purple line for another year, with the current promotion due to end on Nov 30.

data.title: Heavy rain in Northeast, North, Central Plains, East, South early this week
data.description: The Meteorological Department forecast is for fluctuating weather and possible heavy rain in the Northeast, North, Central Plains and East into Tuesday, and persistent rain in the South into Wednesday.

data.title: Laos and Cambodia join forces to boost tourism
data.description: Laos and Cambodia are stepping up tourism cooperation under the slogan “Two Countries, One Destination”, with plans to improve cross-border travel and promote joint tourism routes showcasing their natural attractions and cultural heritage.

data.title: Sri Lankan turbine project fuels anger as fish hauls plunge
data.description: MANNAR (SRI LANKA) - Beneath rotating wind turbines on Sri Lanka's Mannar peninsula, a fishing net is hauled up the beach by tractor winches and 20 men, but once again the catch is meagre.

data.title: Mona Lisa off limits as Paris shuts museums over protest fears
data.description: PARIS - Disappointed tourists ‌poked their heads through the Louvre's locked gates on Saturday, shut off from the Mona Lisa as galleries and museums across Paris closed as a precaution ahead of fresh demonstrations.

data.title: Riyadh airport resumes flights following Houthi attacks
data.description: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia - Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following strikes from Yemen's Houthis on the Saudi capital, though the Iran-backed group warned of more to come.

data.title: Missing Dutch celebrity left Thailand late last year - police
data.description: Missing Dutch television personality and politician Emile Ratelband, whose family is seeking information as to his whereabouts, left Thailand late last year, according to immigration police.

data.title: More Lula, or back to the Bolsonaros? Brazil votes in cliffhanger
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil - Brazilians head to the polls on Sunday facing a stark choice: another four years under veteran leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, or a return to the right under Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

data.title: Yemen's Houthis renew warning against using Riyadh airport
data.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis ​on Sunday renewed their ‌warning against using Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, hours after the airport announced it will designate two terminals for flights following a suspension earlier ​this ⁠month.

data.title: Obama blasts Trump's 'chaos and cruelty' while campaigning for Democrats
data.description: WASHINGTON - Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections.

data.title: Quartet in race for Hong Kong crown
data.description: HONG KONG: The final round of the Hong Kong Open is set for a titanic battle today after American John Catlin and Anirban Lahiri from India, both former Asian Tour No.1s and multiple tournament winners, Belgium star Thomas Pieters and Caleb Surratt, the United States golfer who is one of the hottest young players in the game, took the third-round lead.

data.title: 'No ID, No Ads' looms
data.description: The government is intensifying its crackdown on online scams with a new "No ID, No Ads" policy taking effect on Nov 1.

data.title: Man City's perfect start ended by Aston Villa, Arsenal go joint-top
data.description: LONDON - Manchester City's flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton.

data.title: Thousands protest in Turkey over journalists' arrests, media shutdowns
data.description: ISTANBUL - Thousands rallied in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday against what they described as growing pressure on journalists in Turkey, including arrests, media shutdowns and the appointment of state administrators.
